title: The History of Call of Duty | From World War II to Modern Warfare and Black Ops
description: How Call of Duty grew from a 2003 World War II shooter into the best-selling first-person shooter series ever: Infinity Ward, Modern Warfare, Black Ops and the Microsoft deal.

sections.heading: A shooter that took over
sections.script: Call of Duty is listed by Guinness World Records as the best-selling first-person shooter series ever made, and the franchise has passed five hundred million copies sold. It started life as a World War II game and grew into a yearly event that millions of players wait for. Along the way it has moved through the modern day, the Cold War, the near future and even outer space, and it has gone from consoles and PC to free-to-play and mobile. In this video we go through its history: the original game, the Modern Warfare revolution, Black Ops, the studios behind it, the free games that brought in millions more players, and the huge deal that put it in the hands of Microsoft.

sections.heading: Two thousand three: the original
sections.script: The first Call of Duty was released on October twenty ninth, two thousand three, for Windows. It was made by Infinity Ward, a studio formed by developers who had worked on Medal of Honor Allied Assault, and published by Activision, which later bought the studio. The game was set in World War II, and it was the start of a series that would eventually change online shooters forever. That first release laid the foundation for everything that followed.

sections.heading: More World War II games
sections.script: The series stayed in World War II for its first few games. Infinity Ward made Call of Duty two in two thousand five, which came to PC and the Xbox three sixty, and Treyarch made Call of Duty three in two thousand six. Treyarch returned to the war in two thousand eight with World at War. Each game added bigger battles and more cinematic moments, and the community around the series kept growing.

sections.heading: Two thousand seven: Modern Warfare
sections.script: Then everything changed. In two thousand seven, Call of Duty four Modern Warfare left World War II behind and moved the series into a modern setting. It was the breakthrough title for the series, and it created the Modern Warfare sub-series. Infinity Ward followed it with Modern Warfare two in two thousand nine, and Modern Warfare three came in twenty eleven. These games became hugely popular, and they are still remembered as some of the best in the series. Modern Warfare also shaped how online shooters work. Its multiplayer let you build custom classes with perks, rewarded streaks of kills with support like a UAV, an airstrike or an attack helicopter, and gave you ranks, unlocks and a Prestige system to keep you playing. Modern Warfare two arrived on November tenth, two thousand nine, and Activision reported roughly four point seven million copies sold in North America and the United Kingdom on its first day, a record launch at the time.

sections.heading: Two thousand ten: Black Ops
sections.script: In two thousand ten, Treyarch released Call of Duty Black Ops, which started a second major sub-series. The series went on to include Black Ops two, Black Ops three, Black Ops four, Cold War, and Black Ops six in twenty twenty four, so the line is still going strong. Black Ops four, released on October twelfth, twenty eighteen, was the first mainline Call of Duty without a single-player campaign. Instead, Treyarch added Blackout, a battle royale mode for up to one hundred players, which was described as battle royale the Black Ops way. Then in November twenty twenty, Black Ops Cold War took players to the early nineteen eighties, at the height of the Cold War, with a campaign built around the hunt for an alleged Soviet spy named Perseus. Treyarch led its development, with Raven Software also contributing.

sections.heading: Many studios, one series
sections.script: Today, Call of Duty is made by several studios working in rotation. Infinity Ward, Treyarch and Sledgehammer Games all lead different releases, with Raven Software helping on later Black Ops games. In twenty nineteen, Infinity Ward rebooted Modern Warfare, followed by Modern Warfare two in twenty twenty two and Modern Warfare three in twenty twenty three. This rotation is how the series manages to release a new game every year. That teamwork between studios has let each one bring its own style to the series.

sections.heading: New settings: WWII and space
sections.script: The twenty tens were a time of experiments. In twenty seventeen, Sledgehammer Games brought the series back to World War II with Call of Duty WWII, the first return to that period since World at War in two thousand eight. Only a year earlier, Infinity Ward had sent the series in the opposite direction with Infinite Warfare, set in the year twenty eighty. It was the first game in the series focused on settings beyond Earth, with space battles and zero gravity combat. Fans had strong opinions about both, which shows how much people care about where the series goes next. Infinite Warfare even cast Kit Harington as the villain, Admiral Kotch, and its multiplayer introduced Combat Rigs, specialised suits that matched different playstyles. When Call of Duty WWII was revealed in April twenty seventeen, Sledgehammer's co-founders Michael Condrey and Glen Schofield presented it on a live stream.

sections.heading: Free to play: Mobile and Warzone
sections.script: Call of Duty also found new ways to reach players. On October first, twenty nineteen, Call of Duty Mobile launched on iOS and Android. It was developed by TiMi Studios and published by Activision, and the publisher announced that it had passed thirty five million downloads within days. Then on March tenth, twenty twenty, Call of Duty Warzone arrived as a free-to-play battle royale. Activision announced that it had passed fifty million players in its first month. These free games opened the series to millions of people who had never bought a Call of Duty before.

sections.heading: Record-breaking sales
sections.script: The sales are enormous. In April twenty twenty one, Activision announced that the franchise had passed four hundred million copies sold. A few years later, with Black Ops six on the market, the franchise had passed five hundred million. Guinness World Records lists it as the best-selling first-person shooter series, and it is also one of the best-selling video game franchises of all time. Behind those numbers are millions of friends who log in every year to play together.

sections.heading: The Microsoft deal
sections.script: In January twenty twenty two, Microsoft announced that it would buy Activision Blizzard for sixty eight point seven billion dollars in cash. After reviews by regulators around the world, including the United Kingdom, the deal was completed on October thirteenth, twenty twenty three. That means Call of Duty is now part of Microsoft Gaming, alongside Xbox Game Studios, one of the biggest changes in the history of the series. Microsoft's boss of gaming, Phil Spencer, said the work of bringing Activision franchises to Game Pass and other platforms would begin that day. In July twenty twenty three, Microsoft also agreed a ten year deal with Sony to keep Call of Duty on PlayStation. And Black Ops six, released on October twenty fifth, twenty twenty four, was the first Call of Duty to launch on Xbox Game Pass on day one, while still being sold on PlayStation, Xbox and PC.

sections.heading: Which one is your favourite
sections.script: That was the history of Call of Duty, from a World War II shooter in two thousand three to a giant that sells hundreds of millions of copies, with Modern Warfare, Black Ops, Warzone and many more chapters along the way. Whether you play on console, PC or your phone, there is a Call of Duty for almost every kind of player. Now it is your turn. Which Call of Duty is the best of all time: the original, Modern Warfare, Black Ops, or something newer? Tell us in the comments below, and subscribe to the channel for more gaming history and news.
